_instructions: Score every hint for the pair it sits under. 'already_served' is context only: do not score it.

hints.explanation: The MacBook Air is a thin laptop made by Apple.

lines.AIR: MacBook Air is Apple's lightweight laptop line.

hints.explanation: An airplane and a jet plane are both planes.

lines.JET: A jet plane is a plane powered by jet engines.

hints.explanation: In Avatar: The Last Airbender, the Avatar learns to bend air, water, earth and fire.

lines.AIR: Aang, the Avatar, is an Air Nomad and an airbender.
lines.WATER: The Avatar must also master waterbending, which Katara teaches Aang.

hints.explanation: Christopher Columbus sailed to the Americas in 1492, and Columbus Day is a U.S. holiday named for him.

lines.DAY: Columbus Day is a U.S. holiday held in October.

hints.explanation: Harp seals are named for a harp-shaped marking, and angels are often pictured playing harps.

lines.ANGEL: Angels are often shown playing harps in art.
lines.SEAL: Adult harp seals have a dark harp-shaped marking on their backs.

hints.explanation: Apple stores have a Genius Bar for tech help.

lines.APPLE: The Genius Bar is the help desk inside Apple stores.
lines.GENIUS: Apple's tech support staff at the bar are called Geniuses.

hints.explanation: The pupil is part of the eye, and the apple of one's eye originally meant the pupil.

lines.APPLE: The phrase apple of my eye originally referred to the pupil.
lines.PUPIL: The pupil is the dark opening at the center of the eye.

hints.explanation: A slot machine is nicknamed a one-armed bandit.

lines.ARM: The one-armed bandit is named for the lever arm on its side.
lines.CASINO: One-armed bandits are the slot machines on casino floors.

hints.explanation: Wingspan and arm span both measure from tip to tip.

lines.ARM: Arm span measures fingertip to fingertip with arms stretched out.
lines.WING: Wingspan measures from one wingtip to the other.

hints.explanation: Storks build big nests, and in folklore a stork delivers a new baby.

lines.BABY: In folklore and cartoons, a stork brings a new baby to the family.
lines.NEST: White storks build large nests, often on rooftops and chimneys.

hints.explanation: Labor means work, and a mother in labor is giving birth to a baby.

lines.BABY: Labor is the process of giving birth to a baby.
lines.WORK: Labor is another word for work.

hints.explanation: Mary Poppins carries a carpet bag that holds far more than it should.

lines.BAG: Mary Poppins pulls a hat stand and a lamp out of her bag.
lines.CARPET: Her bag is a carpet bag, made from carpet-like fabric.

hints.explanation: Cork comes from the bark of the cork oak, and Cork is a city in Ireland.

lines.BARK: Cork is harvested from the bark of the cork oak tree.
lines.IRELAND: Cork is a city in the south of Ireland.

hints.explanation: Cinnamon spice comes from tree bark, and it flavors the cinnamon roll.

lines.BARK: Cinnamon is made from the inner bark of cinnamon trees.
lines.ROLL: A cinnamon roll is a sweet roll swirled with cinnamon.

hints.explanation: In basketball slang, a jam is a dunk.

lines.BASKETBALL: Basketball players dunk the ball through the hoop.
lines.JAM: To jam the ball is to dunk it.

hints.explanation: Bed Bath & Beyond is a well-known U.S. home-goods brand.

lines.BATH: Bath is the middle word of Bed Bath & Beyond.
lines.BED: Bed is the first word of Bed Bath & Beyond.

hints.explanation: In legend, Archimedes realized in his bath how to test whether a king's crown was pure gold.

lines.BATH: Legend says Archimedes had his eureka moment while getting into a bath.
lines.CROWN: Archimedes was asked to check whether King Hiero's gold crown had been mixed with silver.

hints.explanation: The city of Bath in England is famous for its ancient Roman baths.

lines.BATH: The Romans built public baths, including the ones that gave Bath its name.
lines.ENGLAND: Bath, England, has some of the best-preserved Roman baths in the world.

hints.explanation: Teddy Roosevelt's motto was "speak softly and carry a big stick," and the teddy bear is named after him.

lines.BEAR: The teddy bear was named after Theodore "Teddy" Roosevelt.
lines.STICK: Teddy Roosevelt summed up his foreign policy as "speak softly and carry a big stick."

hints.explanation: Michael Jackson sang "Beat It" and was famous for wearing a single sparkly glove.

lines.BEAT: "Beat It" is a hit song by Michael Jackson.
lines.GLOVE: Michael Jackson often performed wearing one sequined glove.

hints.explanation: A startled heart "skips a beat," and skipping rope is a classic game.

lines.BEAT: A racing heart is said to skip a beat.
lines.ROPE: Skipping rope means jumping over a swinging rope.

hints.explanation: The Flintstones live in the town of Bedrock.

lines.BED: The Flintstones' hometown, Bedrock, starts with bed.
lines.ROCK: The Flintstones' town Bedrock ends with rock, and flint itself is a rock.

hints.explanation: Angus Young is AC/DC's lead guitarist, and Angus is a famous breed of beef cattle.

lines.BEEF: Angus cattle are prized for their beef.
lines.YOUNG: Angus Young is AC/DC's schoolboy-uniformed lead guitarist.

hints.explanation: Alexander Hamilton is on the $10 bill and was shot in a duel with Aaron Burr.

lines.BILL: Hamilton appears on the U.S. $10 bill.
lines.SHOT: Hamilton was fatally shot in an 1804 duel.

hints.explanation: A sixteenth birthday is famously celebrated as a sweet sixteen.

lines.BIRTHDAY: A sixteenth birthday is often a big party in the U.S., the sweet sixteen.
lines.SWEET: Sixteen is the age of a sweet sixteen.

hints.explanation: People make a wish and blow out the candles on a birthday cake.

lines.BIRTHDAY: Birthday cakes are topped with candles.
lines.WISH: Blowing out the candles comes with making a wish.

hints.explanation: Apple's logo is an apple with a bite taken out, and Apple makes computers.

lines.BITE: The Apple logo shows an apple with a bite missing.
lines.COMPUTER: Apple makes the Mac line of computers.

hints.explanation: Minecraft worlds are built from blocks, and zombies are among its classic monsters.

lines.BLOCK: In Minecraft, the world is made of cube-shaped blocks you can break and place.
lines.ZOMBIE: Zombies are common hostile mobs in Minecraft.

hints.explanation: Royal blood means noble birth, also called blue blood, and royal blue is a color.

lines.BLOOD: Royal blood means descent from kings and queens.
lines.BLUE: Royal blue is a deep bright blue, and blue blood also means aristocracy.

hints.explanation: A lightning bolt strikes in a storm, and "lightning fast" means very quick, fitting for sprinter Usain Bolt.

lines.BOLT: A single strike of lightning is called a bolt.

hints.explanation: Oprah's Book Club turned many of its picks into bestsellers.

lines.BOOK: Books picked for Oprah's Book Club often became bestsellers.
lines.CLUB: Oprah's Book Club began on her talk show in 1996.

hints.explanation: Kiwi is a well-known brand of boot and shoe polish.

lines.BOOT: Kiwi polish is used to shine leather boots.
lines.KIWI: Kiwi polish is named after New Zealand's kiwi bird.

hints.explanation: Bowser is the boss Mario fights at the end of many Mario games.

lines.BOSS: Bowser is the final boss in many Mario games.
lines.MARIO: Bowser kidnaps Princess Peach, and Mario sets out to rescue her.

hints.explanation: A fiddle is a violin, played with a bow.

lines.BOW: A fiddle is played with a bow.
lines.VIOLIN: Fiddle is another name for the violin.

hints.explanation: Cartoon kangaroos are often drawn in boxing gloves, and real male kangaroos box when they fight.

lines.BOX: Male kangaroos box with their forepaws when they spar.
lines.GLOVE: Cartoon boxing kangaroos are usually shown wearing gloves.

hints.explanation: King Arthur's knights sat at the Round Table, and boxing matches are fought in rounds.

lines.BOXING: A boxing match is divided into rounds.
lines.TABLE: King Arthur's knights gathered at the Round Table.

hints.explanation: Wonder Woman is a superhero, and Wonder Bread is a famous sliced bread.

lines.BREAD: Wonder Bread is a well-known brand of sliced white bread.
lines.SUPERHERO: Wonder Woman is a famous DC Comics superhero.

hints.explanation: George Orwell wrote Animal Farm and created Big Brother in Nineteen Eighty-Four.

lines.BROTHER: Big Brother is the all-seeing leader in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.
lines.FARM: Animal Farm is George Orwell's fable about farm animals who revolt.

hints.explanation: In Back to the Future, Doc Brown's dog is named Einstein.

lines.BROWN: Doc Brown is the inventor in Back to the Future.
lines.EINSTEIN: Doc Brown's dog in Back to the Future is named Einstein.

hints.explanation: Bubble wrap protects packages, and Egyptian mummies were wrapped in linen.

lines.BUBBLE: Bubble wrap is a protective packing wrap.
lines.MUMMY: Egyptian mummies were wrapped in strips of linen.

hints.explanation: Boba is another name for bubble tea.

lines.BUBBLE: Bubble tea is also called boba, after its chewy tapioca pearls.
lines.TEA: Boba is a tea drink served with tapioca pearls.

hints.explanation: Wild Bill Hickok and Buffalo Bill Cody were both famous figures of the Old West.

lines.BUFFALO: Buffalo Bill Cody ran a famous Wild West show.
lines.WILD: Wild Bill Hickok was a famous Wild West gunfighter and lawman.

hints.explanation: A sports coach often blows a whistle, and a coach is also a long-distance bus.

lines.BUS: A coach is a bus built for long trips.
lines.WHISTLE: Many sports coaches use a whistle at practice.

hints.explanation: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button is a film about a man who ages backward.

lines.CASE: The title calls Benjamin's story a curious case.

hints.explanation: In Coraline, the Other Mother and her world have buttons for eyes.

lines.BUTTON: The Other Mother wants to sew buttons over Coraline's eyes.
lines.EYE: Coraline's other-world family all have button eyes.

hints.explanation: Pet hamsters usually live in cages and run on exercise wheels.

lines.CAGE: Pet hamsters are commonly kept in cages.
lines.WHEEL: Hamsters are famous for running on exercise wheels.

hints.explanation: Luke Cage is a Marvel superhero, and Luke Skywalker trained with Yoda.

lines.CAGE: Luke Cage is a Marvel superhero with unbreakable skin.
lines.YODA: Yoda trained Luke Skywalker in The Empire Strikes Back.

hints.explanation: The Flash is a speedy DC superhero, and a camera flash lights up a photo.

lines.CAMERA: A camera flash gives a burst of light for a photo.
lines.SUPERHERO: The Flash is a DC Comics superhero with super speed.

hints.explanation: The Skittles slogan invites you to taste the rainbow.

lines.TASTE: The Skittles slogan is Taste the Rainbow.

hints.explanation: Cap'n Crunch is a sweet breakfast cereal.

lines.CAP: Cap'n is short for Captain in Cap'n Crunch.
lines.CEREAL: Cap'n Crunch is a crunchy corn and oat cereal.

hints.explanation: Uppercase letters are capital letters; printers kept them in the upper case of type.

lines.CAPITAL: Capital letters are also called uppercase letters.

hints.explanation: A right hook is a boxing punch, and Captain Hook is Peter Pan's enemy.

lines.CAPTAIN: Captain Hook is the pirate villain of Peter Pan.
lines.RIGHT: A right hook is a curving punch thrown with the right hand.

hints.explanation: SUV stands for sport utility vehicle.

lines.CAR: An SUV is a roomy car-like vehicle.
lines.SPORT: The S in SUV stands for sport.

hints.explanation: FDR's New Deal fought the Great Depression, and card players deal the cards.

lines.CARD: To deal is to hand out playing cards.
lines.NEW: The New Deal was Franklin Roosevelt's 1930s response to the Great Depression.

hints.explanation: A classic snowman has stick arms and a carrot nose.

lines.CARROT: A carrot is the classic snowman nose.
lines.STICK: Snowmen are often given sticks for arms.

hints.explanation: Rice Krispies is a classic Kellogg's breakfast cereal.

lines.CEREAL: Rice Krispies is a breakfast cereal famous for its snap, crackle and pop.
lines.RICE: Rice Krispies are made of crisped rice.

hints.explanation: A chain is made of links, and a chain-link fence is woven from wire.

lines.CHAIN: A chain is a series of connected links.
lines.FENCE: A chain-link fence is made of woven wire in a diamond pattern.

hints.explanation: Chain mail is armor made of linked metal rings, worn by medieval knights.

lines.CHAIN: Chain mail is armor made of small interlocking metal rings.
lines.KNIGHT: Medieval knights often wore mail armor.

hints.explanation: A chain is only as strong as its weakest link.

lines.CHAIN: A chain breaks at its weakest link.
lines.LINK: The weakest link is the one most likely to fail.

hints.explanation: Rearranging the deck chairs on the Titanic means busywork in the face of disaster.

lines.CHAIR: A deck chair is a folding lounge chair for ships and patios.
lines.TITANIC: The saying imagines tidying the Titanic's deck as the ship sinks.

hints.explanation: Charm and top are two of the six flavors of quark.

lines.CHARM: The charm quark is one of six quark flavors.
lines.TOP: The top quark is the heaviest known quark.

hints.explanation: A soulmate is a perfect partner, and checkmate ends a chess game.

lines.CHECK: Checkmate wins a game of chess.
lines.SOUL: A soulmate is a person you feel perfectly matched with.

hints.explanation: People say cheese to smile for a picture.

lines.CHEESE: Saying cheese stretches your mouth into a smile.
lines.PICTURE: Photographers ask you to smile for the picture.

hints.explanation: A clean sweep is a total win, and a chimney sweep cleans chimneys.

lines.CHIMNEY: A chimney sweep clears soot from chimneys.
lines.CLEAN: A clean sweep means winning every game or contest.

hints.explanation: In Britain, Santa Claus is often called Father Christmas.

lines.CHRISTMAS: Santa delivers presents on Christmas Eve.
lines.FATHER: Father Christmas is the traditional British name for Santa.

hints.explanation: Life of Pi is a famous novel and film, and pi links a circle's circumference to its diameter.

lines.CIRCLE: Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
lines.LIFE: Life of Pi is a novel, later a film, about a boy adrift at sea with a tiger.

hints.explanation: To scrub is to clean hard, and nurses often wear scrubs.

lines.CLEAN: To scrub something is to clean it by rubbing hard.
lines.NURSE: Many nurses wear scrubs at work.

hints.explanation: In the Bible, Joseph gets a coat of many colors and is later sold into Egypt, where he rises to power.

lines.COAT: Joseph's father gave him a coat of many colors.
lines.EGYPT: Joseph was sold into slavery in Egypt and became a high official there.

hints.explanation: A turncoat is a traitor.

lines.COAT: Turncoat, a word for a traitor, ends with coat.
lines.TURN: To turn on your own side is what a turncoat does.

hints.explanation: The trench coat is named for the trenches of World War I, where officers wore it.

lines.COAT: The trench coat is a belted raincoat named for WWI trenches.
lines.WAR: Trench warfare defined much of World War I.

hints.explanation: Chicken soup is a classic home remedy for a cold.

lines.COLD: Many people eat chicken soup when they have a cold.
lines.SOUP: Chicken noodle soup is a classic comfort soup.

hints.explanation: A mood ring changes color with temperature.

lines.COLOR: Mood rings shift color as your finger warms or cools.
lines.RING: A mood ring is a ring with a heat-sensitive stone.

hints.explanation: A hard drive is a computer's classic storage device.

lines.COMPUTER: Many computers store their files on a hard drive.
lines.HARD: A hard drive is named for its rigid spinning disks.

hints.explanation: Train conductors have long punched passengers' paper tickets.

lines.CONDUCTOR: A train conductor checks and collects tickets.
lines.PUNCH: A ticket punch clips a hole in a paper ticket.

hints.explanation: Eli Whitney invented the cotton gin, and Whitney Houston sang "I Will Always Love You."

lines.COTTON: Eli Whitney patented the cotton gin in 1794.
lines.LOVE: Whitney Houston had a huge hit with "I Will Always Love You."

hints.explanation: Brand-new means completely new, and ranchers brand cattle to mark ownership.

lines.COW: Ranchers brand cows to show who owns them.
lines.NEW: Something brand-new has never been used.

hints.explanation: Wedding Crashers is a comedy about uninvited guests, and a wedding party is the couple's attendants.

lines.CRASH: In the film Wedding Crashers, two men crash weddings.
lines.PARTY: A wedding party is the group of attendants at a wedding.

hints.explanation: A group of crows is called a murder, and detectives solve murders.

lines.CROW: A flock of crows is called a murder.
lines.DETECTIVE: Detectives in mystery stories solve murders.

hints.explanation: In Arthurian legend, knights quest for the Holy Grail, a sacred cup.

lines.CUP: The Holy Grail is usually described as a cup.
lines.KNIGHT: The Knights of the Round Table set out to find the Grail.

hints.explanation: To pass the buck is to shift the blame, and a buck is a male deer.

lines.DEER: A buck is a male deer.
lines.PASS: To pass the buck means to hand responsibility to someone else.

hints.explanation: The monk seal is an endangered seal, and Monk is a TV detective series.

lines.DETECTIVE: Adrian Monk is the detective in the TV series Monk.
lines.SEAL: Monk seals live in Hawaii and the Mediterranean.

hints.explanation: Natural history museums are famous for their dinosaur skeletons.

lines.DINOSAUR: Many natural history museums show mounted dinosaur fossils.
lines.HISTORY: A natural history museum displays the history of life and the Earth.

hints.explanation: Dawn is a dish soap brand, and dawn is the first light of morning.

lines.DISH: Dawn is a well-known brand of dish soap.
lines.MORNING: Dawn is the first light of the morning.

hints.explanation: Radio telescopes collect signals from space with huge dish antennas.

lines.DISH: Many radio telescopes are giant dish antennas.
lines.RADIO: A radio telescope studies space by picking up radio waves.

hints.explanation: Downward dog is a classic yoga pose.

lines.DOG: Downward dog is named after a dog's stretch.
lines.DOWN: Downward dog points the hips up and the head down.

hints.explanation: The 1992 U.S. Olympic basketball team was nicknamed the Dream Team.

lines.DREAM: The Dream Team featured Michael Jordan and Magic Johnson.
lines.TEAM: The Dream Team won Olympic gold in Barcelona.

hints.explanation: Cinderella's fairy godmother gives her a ball gown and turns a pumpkin into a coach.

lines.DRESS: Cinderella's fairy godmother conjures her a dress for the ball.
lines.PUMPKIN: Cinderella's coach is made from a pumpkin.

hints.explanation: In Alice in Wonderland, Alice follows the White Rabbit and drinks from a bottle labeled DRINK ME.

lines.DRINK: Alice shrinks after drinking from a bottle labeled DRINK ME.
lines.RABBIT: Alice follows the White Rabbit down the rabbit hole.

hints.explanation: In Disney's Snow White, the Seven Dwarfs sing Heigh-Ho as they head home from the mine.

lines.DWARF: The Seven Dwarfs march home from work to the song Heigh-Ho.
lines.MINE: The dwarfs work in a diamond mine and sing Heigh-Ho on the way home.

hints.explanation: In Disney's Snow White, the dwarfs sing "Heigh-Ho," with the line "it's off to work we go."

lines.DWARF: The Seven Dwarfs sing "Heigh-Ho" in Disney's Snow White.
lines.WORK: The song "Heigh-Ho" goes "it's off to work we go."

hints.explanation: In cartoons, someone strikes a match to light the fuse on a stick of dynamite.

lines.DYNAMITE: Cartoon dynamite sticks come with a burning fuse.
lines.MATCH: A lit match can light a fuse.

hints.explanation: Pizza comes in thin crust, and Earth's crust is the planet's thin rocky outer layer.

lines.EARTH: Earth's crust is a thin rocky shell compared with the planet's size.
lines.THIN: Thin crust is a popular style of pizza.

hints.explanation: Einstein worked as a clerk in the Swiss patent office when he published his famous 1905 papers.

lines.EINSTEIN: Albert Einstein worked at the patent office in Bern, Switzerland.
lines.OFFICE: A patent office reviews applications for inventions.

hints.explanation: The History Channel is a TV network, and the English Channel separates England from France.

lines.ENGLAND: The English Channel lies between southern England and France.
lines.HISTORY: The History Channel is a cable TV network about the past.

hints.explanation: A facepalm shows disbelief, and a palm tree is a tropical tree.

lines.FACE: A facepalm is putting your palm to your face in dismay.
lines.TREE: Palm trees grow in warm climates.

hints.explanation: Foul play is the opposite of fair play, and a hit baseball lands fair or foul.

lines.FAIR: A batted baseball is ruled fair or foul.
lines.PLAY: Foul play means cheating or a crime.

hints.explanation: In many tellings of Chicken Little, an acorn falls on her head and she thinks the sky is falling.

lines.FALL: An acorn falls on her head and starts the panic.
lines.SKY: Chicken Little thinks the sky is falling.

hints.explanation: The Fast & Furious films famously revolve around family.

lines.FAMILY: Dom Toretto's talk about family is a running theme of Fast & Furious.
lines.FAST: Fast is the first word of Fast & Furious, a street-racing series.

hints.explanation: A fan spins its blades, and grass grows in blades.

lines.FAN: Most fans spin blades to move air.
lines.GRASS: A single leaf of grass is called a blade.

hints.explanation: Sports fans do "the wave" in stadiums, and surfers ride ocean waves.

lines.FAN: Stadium fans do "the wave" by standing up in sequence.

hints.explanation: Sonic means relating to sound, and Sonic the Hedgehog is famous for being fast.

lines.FAST: Sonic the Hedgehog is a video game hero known for super speed.
lines.SOUND: Sonic means having to do with sound, as in a sonic boom.

hints.explanation: A Catholic priest serves God and is addressed as Father.

lines.FATHER: Catholic priests are addressed as Father.
lines.GOD: A priest leads worship of God.

hints.explanation: The Sundance Kid was a Wild West outlaw, and Sundance is a famous film festival.

lines.FILM: The Sundance Film Festival showcases independent films.
lines.KID: The Sundance Kid rode with Butch Cassidy.

hints.explanation: The periodic table lists the chemical elements, and fire was one of the four classical elements.

lines.FIRE: Ancient Greeks counted fire as an element, along with earth, air and water.
lines.TABLE: The periodic table organizes the chemical elements.

hints.explanation: FLOTUS is short for First Lady of the United States.

lines.FIRST: The F in FLOTUS stands for First.
lines.LADY: The L in FLOTUS stands for Lady.

hints.explanation: George Washington was the first U.S. president.

lines.FIRST: Washington was the first president of the United States.
lines.WASHINGTON: George Washington served as president from 1789 to 1797.

hints.explanation: A lightning bolt is a bright flash, and a thunderbolt is lightning with its thunder.

lines.FLASH: A bolt of lightning appears as a sudden flash.
lines.THUNDER: A thunderbolt is a lightning bolt together with its thunder.

hints.explanation: A force field is sci-fi protection, and a magnet is surrounded by a magnetic field.

lines.FORCE: A force field is an invisible barrier in science fiction.
lines.MAGNET: A magnet creates a magnetic field around it.

hints.explanation: In The Little Mermaid, Ariel combs her hair with a fork she calls a dinglehopper.

lines.FORK: Scuttle tells Ariel a fork is a dinglehopper.
lines.HAIR: Ariel uses the fork to comb her hair.

hints.explanation: People toss a coin into a wishing well or a fountain and make a wish.

lines.FOUNTAIN: People toss coins into fountains, famously Rome's Trevi Fountain.
lines.WELL: People toss coins into a wishing well for luck.

hints.explanation: In the 1931 Frankenstein film, a mob of villagers with torches hunts the monster.

lines.FRANKENSTEIN: The mob chases Frankenstein's monster to a windmill.
lines.TORCH: The villagers in the mob carry torches.

hints.explanation: Tony the Tiger is the mascot of Frosted Flakes.

lines.FROST: Tony the Tiger sells Frosted Flakes cereal.
lines.TIGER: Tony is a cartoon tiger who says the cereal is great.

hints.explanation: Jack Frost is the folklore figure of winter cold, and Titanic's Jack dies in the icy Atlantic.

lines.FROST: Jack Frost personifies frost and freezing weather in folklore.
lines.TITANIC: In Titanic, Jack Dawson dies in the freezing water after the ship sinks.

hints.explanation: The funny bone is at the elbow, and "elbow grease" means hard work.

lines.FUNNY: The "funny bone" is a nerve that runs past the elbow.
lines.GREASE: "Elbow grease" is slang for hard physical effort.

hints.explanation: A tongue twister is hard to say, and Twister is a classic party game.

lines.GAME: Twister is a party game played on a mat of colored spots.
lines.TONGUE: A tongue twister is a phrase that is hard to say quickly.

hints.explanation: Heaven's entrance is popularly called the pearly gates.

lines.GATE: The pearly gates are the gates of heaven in popular imagery.
lines.PEARL: In the Book of Revelation, each gate of the heavenly city is made of a single pearl.

hints.explanation: Charlie wins a golden ticket in Willy Wonka's story, and the Golden Gate Bridge is San Francisco's landmark.

lines.GATE: The Golden Gate is the strait spanned by San Francisco's famous bridge.
lines.TICKET: In Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, five golden tickets win a factory tour.

hints.explanation: A kid is a young goat, and kid gloves are made from soft goatskin.

lines.GLOVE: Kid gloves are made of soft leather from young goats.
lines.KID: A baby goat is called a kid.

hints.explanation: In Roman myth, Mercury is the messenger god.

lines.GOD: Mercury serves as the messenger of the gods.
lines.MERCURY: Mercury, the messenger, is shown with winged sandals and a winged hat.

hints.explanation: Kratos is the hero of the God of War video games.

lines.GOD: Kratos becomes the new God of War at the end of the first game.
lines.WAR: God of War is the title of Kratos's video game series.

hints.explanation: A sugar rush is a burst of energy from sweets, and the Gold Rush brought prospectors to California.

lines.GOLD: The California Gold Rush began in 1848.
lines.SUGAR: "Sugar rush" is the popular term for a burst of energy after eating sweets.

hints.explanation: In golf, you sink a putt into the hole.

lines.GOLF: A putt is a gentle golf stroke on the green.
lines.SINK: To sink a putt is to roll it into the cup.

hints.explanation: Keratin is the tough protein that hair and nails are made of.

lines.HAIR: Hair is made mostly of keratin.
lines.NAIL: Fingernails are made mostly of keratin.

hints.explanation: Michael Myers is the masked killer in the Halloween films, and Mike Myers voices Shrek.

lines.HALLOWEEN: Michael Myers is the villain of the Halloween horror films.
lines.SHREK: Mike Myers is the voice of Shrek.

hints.explanation: Sister Sledge sang "We Are Family," and a sledge is a heavy hammer.

lines.HAMMER: A sledge, or sledgehammer, is a big heavy hammer.
lines.SISTER: Sister Sledge is the group behind "We Are Family."

hints.explanation: A powerful batter or boxer can be called a hard hitter or a heavy hitter.

lines.HARD: A hard hitter strikes the ball, or an opponent, with real force.
lines.HEAVY: A heavy hitter is a powerful batter, or by extension an influential person.

hints.explanation: Hard Rock Cafe is a restaurant chain known for its rock-and-roll memorabilia.

lines.HARD: Hard is the first word of Hard Rock Cafe.
lines.ROCK: Rock is the middle word of Hard Rock Cafe, whose walls display rock memorabilia.

hints.explanation: In The Wizard of Oz, the Tin Man wants a heart.

lines.HEART: The Tin Man asks the Wizard for a heart.
lines.MAN: The Tin Man is a man made of tin.

hints.explanation: In The Wizard of Oz, Dorothy's house lands on a witch, and she clicks her heels to go home.

lines.HEEL: Dorothy clicks her heels together three times to return home.
lines.HOUSE: Dorothy's house lands on the Wicked Witch of the East.

hints.explanation: Hockey goalies wear masks to protect their faces.

lines.MASK: A goalie mask protects the face from pucks.

hints.explanation: To darn is to mend a hole in a sock by weaving stitches across it.

lines.HOLE: Darning fills a hole with woven stitches.
lines.SOCK: People darn socks that wear through at the heel or toe.

hints.explanation: Robin is Batman's superhero partner, and Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw.

lines.HOOD: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest.
lines.SUPERHERO: Robin is the costumed sidekick of Batman.

hints.explanation: Captain Hook and Peter Pan battle in Neverland.

lines.HOOK: Captain Hook is the pirate captain of Neverland.
lines.PAN: Peter Pan lives in Neverland with the Lost Boys.

hints.explanation: Horned helmets are a popular Viking image, though real Viking helmets did not have horns.

lines.HORN: Costume Viking helmets usually have horns on them.
lines.VIKING: Vikings are often drawn in horned helmets, an image popularized in the 1800s.

hints.explanation: In Harry Potter, Dobby the house-elf is freed when he is given a sock.

lines.HOUSE: Dobby is a house-elf who served the Malfoy family.
lines.SOCK: Harry tricks Lucius Malfoy into giving Dobby a sock, which frees him.

hints.explanation: Mochi ice cream wraps a ball of ice cream in soft, chewy rice dough.

lines.ICE CREAM: Mochi ice cream is a scoop of ice cream wrapped in a mochi shell.
lines.RICE: Mochi is made from sticky, glutinous rice.

hints.explanation: Soft serve is ice cream dispensed from a machine.

lines.ICE CREAM: Soft serve is a kind of ice cream.
lines.SOFT: Soft serve is softer than scooped ice cream.

hints.explanation: SpongeBob's best friend is Patrick Star, and Saint Patrick is Ireland's patron saint.

lines.IRELAND: Saint Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland.
lines.SPONGE: SpongeBob, a sea sponge, is best friends with Patrick Star.

hints.explanation: Florence Nightingale, a pioneer of modern nursing, was named after Florence, Italy, where she was born.

lines.ITALY: Florence is a city in Italy and Nightingale's birthplace.
lines.NURSE: Florence Nightingale is famous as a founder of modern nursing.

hints.explanation: A paper jam stops a printer.

lines.JAM: A paper jam is paper stuck inside a machine.
lines.PRINTER: Printers can jam when paper gets stuck.

hints.explanation: Michael Jordan starred in the 1996 film Space Jam.

lines.JAM: Jordan headlined Space Jam, and was famous for his jams on the court.
lines.SPACE: Space Jam teams Jordan with the Looney Tunes against alien invaders.

hints.explanation: Sake is a traditional Japanese drink brewed from rice.

lines.JAPAN: Sake is a traditional drink of Japan, often called rice wine.
lines.RICE: Sake is brewed from polished rice.

hints.explanation: Jam is jelly's fruity cousin, and Pearl Jam is a famous rock band.

lines.JELLY: Jam and jelly are both sweet fruit spreads.
lines.PEARL: Pearl Jam is a rock band from Seattle.

hints.explanation: In West Side Story, the Jets and the Sharks are rival New York gangs.

lines.JET: The Jets are the Sharks' rival gang.
lines.NEW YORK: West Side Story is set on the streets of New York City.

hints.explanation: Boxing is the sport of punching, and male kangaroos spar in a way people call boxing.

lines.KANGAROO: Male kangaroos spar with each other, and people call it boxing.
lines.PUNCH: Boxing is built around the punch.

hints.explanation: A Swiss Army knife folds many tools into one pocket knife.

lines.KNIFE: A Swiss Army knife is a folding pocket knife.
lines.TOOL: A Swiss Army knife packs tools like a screwdriver and scissors.

hints.explanation: Lady Justice is shown holding a set of scales.

lines.LADY: Lady Justice is often shown blindfolded with a sword.
lines.SCALE: Lady Justice's scales stand for weighing the evidence.

hints.explanation: A Star Wars lightsaber is often described as a laser sword.

lines.LASER: Fans often call a lightsaber a laser sword.
lines.SWORD: A lightsaber is wielded like a sword.

hints.explanation: A whistle-blower exposes wrongdoing, and a leaf blower clears fallen leaves.

lines.LEAF: A leaf blower uses a blast of air to move leaves.
lines.WHISTLE: A whistle-blower reports wrongdoing inside an organization.

hints.explanation: LEGO pieces are bricks, and a badly missed basketball shot is called a brick.

lines.SHOT: A basketball shot that clangs off the rim is called a brick.

hints.explanation: The Westminster Dog Show is a famous U.S. dog show, and Westminster is an area of central London.

lines.LONDON: Westminster, home of Parliament and Westminster Abbey, is in central London.
lines.SHOW: The Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show is a famous annual U.S. dog show.

hints.explanation: Old radios and TVs used vacuum tubes, and the Tube is London's subway.

lines.LONDON: The London Underground is nicknamed the Tube.
lines.VACUUM: A vacuum tube controls electric current in old electronics.

hints.explanation: Opposite magnetic poles attract, and "opposites attract" is also said about love.

lines.MAGNET: Opposite poles of two magnets attract each other.

hints.explanation: Mario Kart is Nintendo's kart racing series.

lines.MARIO: Mario stars in the Mario Kart games.

hints.explanation: In tennis, match point is the point that can win the whole match.

lines.MATCH: Match point is the point that can decide a match.
lines.TENNIS: Tennis players win games by winning points, and match point can end it.

hints.explanation: Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature.

lines.MERCURY: Mercury is liquid at room temperature.
lines.METAL: Mercury is one of very few metals that are liquid near room temperature.

hints.explanation: "Don't cry over spilled milk" is an old saying, and to "spill the tea" is to share gossip.

lines.MILK: "No use crying over spilled milk" means don't fret about the past.
lines.TEA: To "spill the tea" is slang for sharing gossip.

hints.explanation: A "plant" and a "mole" are both slang for a spy placed inside an organization.

lines.MOLE: A mole is a spy who works from inside an organization.
lines.PLANT: A plant is a spy secretly placed inside a group.

hints.explanation: Neil Young is a rock legend, and Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon.

lines.MOON: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon, in 1969.
lines.YOUNG: Neil Young is a Canadian-born singer-songwriter.

hints.explanation: Nail polish is also called nail enamel, and enamel is the hard outer layer of a tooth.

lines.NAIL: Nail polish is also sold as nail enamel.
lines.TOOTH: Enamel is the hard outer coating of a tooth.

hints.explanation: Robins lay their eggs in a nest, and money saved for later is a nest egg.

lines.NEST: A nest holds a bird's eggs, and savings are called a nest egg.
lines.ROBIN: Robins lay blue eggs, the source of the color robin's-egg blue.

hints.explanation: Fresh means new, and The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air starred Will Smith.

lines.NEW: Fresh is a synonym for new.
lines.PRINCE: The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air was a 1990s sitcom starring Will Smith.

hints.explanation: New York's nickname is the Empire State.

lines.NEW YORK: New York is nicknamed the Empire State.
lines.STATE: The Empire State Building takes its name from New York's state nickname.

hints.explanation: The Bronx Zoo is in New York City.

lines.NEW YORK: The Bronx is one of New York City's five boroughs.
lines.ZOO: The Bronx Zoo is one of the largest city zoos in the U.S.

hints.explanation: Ramen is a Japanese noodle soup.

lines.NOODLE: Ramen is made with wheat noodles.
lines.SOUP: Ramen noodles are served in a hot broth.

hints.explanation: Microsoft Word is part of Microsoft Office, and a password is a pass plus a word.

lines.OFFICE: Microsoft Word is part of the Microsoft Office suite.
lines.PASS: Pass and word together make password.

hints.explanation: A gusher is an oil well that sprays oil out uncontrolled.

lines.OIL: A gusher sends crude oil shooting into the air.
lines.WELL: A gusher is a well that erupts on its own pressure.

hints.explanation: Ernest Hemingway wrote The Old Man and the Sea.

lines.OLD: Hemingway's old man is the fisherman Santiago.
lines.SEA: Hemingway's novella follows Santiago's long struggle at sea with a giant marlin.

hints.explanation: The goddess Athena's symbols include the olive tree and the owl.

lines.OLIVE: In Greek myth, Athena gave Athens the olive tree.
lines.OWL: The owl is a symbol of Athena, goddess of wisdom.

hints.explanation: Palm Sunday falls one week before Easter Sunday.

lines.PALM: Palm Sunday begins Holy Week, the week before Easter.
lines.SUNDAY: Easter is celebrated on a Sunday.

hints.explanation: A tight spiral is the classic football pass, and spiral stairs wind around a center post.

lines.PASS: Quarterbacks throw a spinning football pass called a spiral.
lines.STAIRS: A spiral staircase winds around a central column.

hints.explanation: Relay runners pass a baton, and the Olympic torch relay passes the flame along by hand.

lines.PASS: In a relay race, runners pass a baton to teammates.
lines.TORCH: The Olympic torch relay carries the flame from one torchbearer to the next.

hints.explanation: Leo Tolstoy wrote the epic novel War and Peace.

lines.PEACE: Peace is the second half of Tolstoy's title War and Peace.
lines.WAR: Tolstoy's War and Peace is set during the Napoleonic wars.

hints.explanation: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers, and the Pied Piper led the rats out of Hamelin.

lines.PEPPER: The tongue twister goes "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers."
lines.RAT: The Pied Piper played his pipe to lure the rats out of Hamelin.

hints.explanation: A cell is a small room, as in a prison, and a cell phone is a mobile phone.

lines.PHONE: A cell phone is a mobile phone.
lines.ROOM: A prison cell is a small room.

hints.explanation: Domino tiles are marked with spots, and the Domino's pizza logo is a domino with three spots.

lines.PIZZA: Domino's is a big pizza delivery chain.
lines.SPOT: Each domino tile is marked with spots, or pips.

hints.explanation: Nintendo makes the Switch console, and Pokémon games are released on Nintendo systems.

lines.POKEMON: Pokémon games are released on Nintendo consoles.
lines.SWITCH: The Nintendo Switch is a game console.

hints.explanation: In many U.S. stores, orange sweet potatoes are labeled yams.

lines.POTATO: A true yam is a different plant, though sweet potatoes are often called yams.
lines.SWEET: Orange sweet potatoes are often sold as yams in the U.S.

hints.explanation: Muhammad Ali's "rope-a-dope" tactic is famous, and "Prince Ali" is a song from Aladdin.

lines.PRINCE: "Prince Ali" is the song the Genie sings in Disney's Aladdin.
lines.ROPE: Ali's "rope-a-dope" meant leaning on the ropes to tire out his opponent.

hints.explanation: The Muppets, Jim Henson's puppets, starred in The Muppet Show.

lines.PUPPET: The Muppets are puppets created by Jim Henson.
lines.SHOW: The Muppet Show was a TV variety show starring the Muppets.

hints.explanation: A sock hop was a 1950s school dance, and rabbits hop.

lines.SOCK: At a sock hop, dancers took off their shoes and danced in socks.

hints.explanation: In Aesop's fable, a slow tortoise beats the hare in a race.

lines.RACE: The hare loses the race after stopping for a nap.
lines.TURTLE: A tortoise, a kind of turtle, beats the hare by plodding on.

hints.explanation: KFC's Original Recipe of 11 herbs and spices is a famous trade secret.

lines.RECIPE: KFC's Original Recipe is said to use 11 herbs and spices.
lines.SECRET: KFC guards its chicken recipe as a secret.

hints.explanation: Red Bull's famous slogan says it gives you wings.

lines.RED: Red is the first word of Red Bull, the energy drink.
lines.WING: Red Bull's slogan promises to give you wings.

hints.explanation: New York is the Empire State, and Rome ruled the Roman Empire.

lines.ROME: Rome was the capital of the Roman Empire.
lines.STATE: New York is nicknamed the Empire State.

hints.explanation: A misfit is called a square peg in a round hole.

lines.ROUND: A round hole will not fit a square peg.
lines.SQUARE: A square peg cannot fit a round hole.

hints.explanation: Windsurfing uses a board with a sail that catches the wind.

lines.SURFING: Windsurfing is surfing with a sail, powered by wind.

hints.explanation: Glass is made by melting sand, and windows are made of glass.

lines.SAND: Most glass is made by melting sand at high heat.
lines.WINDOW: Windows are fitted with panes of glass.

hints.explanation: Drawing the short straw means getting the bad job, and scarecrows are traditionally stuffed with straw.

lines.SCARECROW: A scarecrow is traditionally stuffed with straw.
lines.SHORT: To draw the short straw is to be picked for an unwelcome task.

hints.explanation: Male elephant seals have a trunk-like nose, and elephants have trunks.

lines.SEAL: Elephant seals are named for the males' large, trunk-like noses.
lines.TRUNK: An elephant's trunk is its long nose.

hints.explanation: Dolly Parton sang "9 to 5" about the working day, and Dolly the sheep was a famous cloned mammal.

lines.SHEEP: Dolly the sheep, born in 1996, was cloned from an adult cell.
lines.WORK: Dolly Parton's hit "9 to 5" is about working nine to five.

hints.explanation: A heat shield protects a spacecraft on reentry, and a heat wave is a stretch of very hot weather.

lines.SHIELD: A heat shield protects a spacecraft from heat as it returns through the atmosphere.
lines.WAVE: A heat wave is a stretch of unusually hot weather.

hints.explanation: Long John Silver is the pirate of Treasure Island.

lines.SILVER: Long John Silver is the cook-turned-pirate of Treasure Island.
lines.TREASURE: Treasure Island is Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate adventure novel.

hints.explanation: Disney's Frozen follows sisters Anna and Elsa and their snowman friend Olaf.

lines.SISTER: Anna and Elsa are sisters in Frozen.
lines.SNOWMAN: Olaf is the talking snowman in Frozen.

hints.explanation: In Macbeth, the three witches are called the Weird Sisters.

lines.SISTER: The witches in Macbeth are known as the Weird Sisters.
lines.WITCH: Three witches tell Macbeth he will be king.

hints.explanation: A slow clap builds into applause, and a sudden boom of thunder is a thunderclap.

lines.SLOW: A slow clap is applause that starts slowly and builds.
lines.THUNDER: A sudden loud crack of thunder is called a thunderclap.

hints.explanation: Sandy Cheeks, SpongeBob's friend, is a squirrel from Texas.

lines.SQUIRREL: Sandy is a squirrel who lives under the sea in an air-filled dome.

hints.explanation: Kids learn the times table, and Times Square is in New York City.

lines.SQUARE: Times Square is a famous intersection in New York City.
lines.TABLE: A times table lists multiplication facts.

hints.explanation: Gandalf, the wizard of The Lord of the Rings, carries a wizard's staff.

lines.STAFF: Gandalf carries a staff wherever he travels.
lines.WIZARD: Gandalf is the best-known wizard in The Lord of the Rings.

hints.explanation: The Empire Strikes Back is the second Star Wars film released.

lines.STAR WARS: The Empire is the villainous regime in Star Wars.
lines.STRIKE: The Empire strikes back in the title of the 1980 film.

hints.explanation: Storm, a member of the X-Men, can control the weather.

lines.STORM: Storm is one of the X-Men.
lines.WEATHER: Storm can summon wind, rain and lightning.

hints.explanation: A loved one is a sweetheart, and hearts are the classic Valentine's symbol.

lines.SWEET: A sweetheart is someone you love.
lines.VALENTINE: Valentine's cards and candy boxes are often heart-shaped.

hints.explanation: A circuit breaker is a switch that trips to cut the power.

lines.SWITCH: A circuit breaker works as an automatic switch.

hints.explanation: Remote work is a job done away from the office, and a remote changes TV channels.

lines.TELEVISION: A remote control changes channels on a television.
lines.WORK: Remote work means doing your job from home or elsewhere.

hints.explanation: A very skinny person is "thin as a rail," and trains run on rails.

lines.THIN: "Thin as a rail" means very skinny.

hints.explanation: Paper-thin means extremely thin, and wallpaper is paper pasted on a wall.

lines.WALL: Wallpaper is decorative paper applied to walls.

hints.explanation: Old steam trains blew loud steam whistles.

lines.TRAIN: Steam trains are powered by steam engines.
lines.WHISTLE: A steam whistle sounds when steam is forced through it.

hints.explanation: A famous legend says young George Washington chopped a cherry tree.

lines.TREE: In the tale, Washington damages a cherry tree and admits it.
lines.WASHINGTON: The cherry tree story was popularized by biographer Parson Weems.

hints.explanation: In Alice in Wonderland, the White Rabbit checks his pocket watch and frets about being late.

lines.WATCH: The White Rabbit pulls a watch from his waistcoat pocket.
lines.WHITE: Alice follows the White Rabbit down the rabbit hole.

hints.explanation: In Narnia, the White Witch makes it always winter and never Christmas.

lines.WINTER: Under the White Witch, Narnia is stuck in endless winter.
lines.WITCH: The White Witch rules Narnia at the start of the story.
